Millet_Sheaf.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Image 1 is the CURRENT sheaf to REVISE. Image 2 is the Medieval Overhaul wheat sheaf, the PRIMARY composition/density/volume reference. The current sheaf has only three exposed stems and looks like a bouquet; REPLACE that composition with a BIG DENSE HARVEST BUNDLE like image 2. Broad compact fan-shaped upper half formed from MANY closely packed overlapping ears, approximately 9-12 stalks suggested by the outer edge, with almost NO gaps and almost NO exposed individual stems. The whole upper mass is one unified solid silhouette: show only a few broad contour lobes identifying crop, not each individual grain or ear. Binding band directly under the dense head mass at the narrow waist, and one thick short sheaf base flaring below the band. Lower cut stalks should be one broad mass, not three separate sticks. Overall width comparable to height, squat full bundle rather than tall thin bouquet. Very simple flat muted ochre gold fill with medium ochre-brown contour and one brown binding band, at most 3 fill colors. Match the low detail of image 2. NO interior grain lines, NO realistic detail, NO leaves, NO bow, NO gradients, NO shading, NO texture, NO background/ground/shadow/text. One isolated transparent sprite on square canvas with 7% margins. Readable at 64px. MIXED millet bundle: the upper silhouette combines long rounded foxtail AWA tops, shorter compact lobed HIE tops, and a few broader branched KIBI tops. All three types intermixed in one densely packed mass, not just three separated stalks. Preserve distinguishable silhouettes only around the outer edge. Ochre-gold seed mass and stalk base.
